tier_reason: Upgraded D to C: the coost v3 docs (archived in the coostdocs/coostdocs.github.io repo at commit deb7584, Mar 2024, pages en/co/other/fastream/ and cn/co/other/fastream/) state that fastream is 'about 10~30 times faster than snprintf on different platforms' and that std::ostringstream 'may be several times slower than snprintf' (the Chinese page says measured). That is a first-party number with no workload, compiler, flags, CPU or results table; fastring itself has benchmark code against std::string (v3.0.2 test/str.cc, master benchmark/string.cc) but no published numbers.

corrections.claimed_speedup: fastream: 'about 10~30 times faster than snprintf on different platforms'; the same page says std::ostringstream 'may be several times slower than snprintf' (coost v3 docs, first-party, no methodology). fastring: no numbers against std::string anywhere found.
corrections.baseline: snprintf and std::ostringstream (fastream); std::string (fastring, benchmark code only, no published numbers)
corrections.workload: Unstated. fastream is an append-only char stream meant to replace std::ostringstream/snprintf for building strings (its number formatting uses coost's fast::u64toa/u64toh/dtoa, which v3.0.2 test/fast.cc times against snprintf with no published results). fastring/co::string vs std::string assign and find micro-benchmarks exist as code only (v3.0.2 test/str.cc, master benchmark/string.cc).
corrections.caveats: Only number is the coost v3 docs sentence '10~30 times faster than snprintf on different platforms' (first-party, no workload, compiler, flags, CPU or table); it is gone from the current docs, which were rewritten for coost v4 (Sep-Oct 2026) and make no performance claim for co::string. No published fastream benchmark against snprintf or std::ostringstream was found (v3.0.2 test/fast.cc only times the u64toa/u64toh/dtoa primitives against snprintf; the benchmark branch has only json_bm.cc and log_bm.cc). fastring has no numbers against std::string; v3.0.2 test/str.cc and master benchmark/string.cc (std::string vs co::string assign and find) publish no results. fastring.h and fastream.h were removed in v4.0.0 (2026-09-15; raw fetch at HEAD returns 404) and exist only up to tag v3.0.2 (2023-11-23); master has co::string in include/co/string.h, which uses coost's own allocator. Not standalone headers: they depend on coost's fast.h and memory allocator.

notes: Record's 'no numbers anywhere' was wrong: the v3 docs (reachable via raw.githubusercontent.com on the coostdocs/coostdocs.github.io repo history, since *.github.io is blocked) claim fastream is 10~30x faster than snprintf, so tier moves D to C, but the baseline is snprintf/std::ostringstream rather than the category's std::string, and fastring vs std::string has code but no numbers. The components were removed in coost v4.0.0 (replaced by co::string), so the lead is historical; metadata checked: MIT (LICENSE.md), 4.2k stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-09-28 (tag v4.0.1). Same repo already listed for co/json and co/log (separate ids), not a duplicate of those.
